posts.content:
Today, we are excited to launch v6.7

See what's inside https://lnkd.in/evi59-wb

- Cal.com Notes
Your Cal Video calls now write their own recap. Whenever a meeting is transcribed, Cal.com automatically turns that transcript into a clear, readable summary of what was discussed.

- Cal Pay (powered by Whop)

Getting paid just got a lot simpler. Cal Pay is now available to everyone by default, so there's no trip to the App Store and no "Install" step to worry about.

- Private event notes

Now you can leave yourself (and your team) notes on an event that your guests will never see. Add a private note to an event type and it appears on the host's calendar event while invitees still get the normal, polished description.

… and tons of new improvements:

- We fixed a bug where toggling "Add all team members" on a round-robin event would wipe your hand-picked fixed hosts.
- We added an opt-in setting that hides the previous host's "Who"/"Where" details (and ICS meeting data) from reassignment cancellation emails.
- We added a "Sync on" badge to connected calendar accounts that have an active watch subscription.
- We added support for ?duration= on dynamic group links (username+username/dynamic), locking the booker to that single duration.
- We added an option to exclude weekends when computing the CRM record-owner fallback window.
- We split the workflows and routing forms lists into Personal and Team tabs.
- We refreshed the forgot-password flow in our UI.
- We now block saving an event type whose paid price falls below Stripe's per-currency minimum charge.
- We added a new slotsFetchedembed event that emits available slots on initial load and on every refetch (month, date, duration, or timezone change).
- We added Cloudflare Turnstile and a 45-second resend cooldown to workflow phone verification to curb SMS pumping and toll fraud.

posts.content:
Open source is dead.

That’s not a statement we ever thought we’d make.

Cal.com was built on open source. It shaped our product, our community, and our growth. But the world has changed faster than our principles could keep up.

AI has fundamentally altered the security landscape. What once required time, expertise, and intent can now be automated at scale. Code is no longer just read. It is scanned, mapped, and exploited. Near zero cost.

In that world, transparency becomes exposure. Especially at scale.

After a lot of deliberation, we’ve made the decision to close the core Cal.com codebase.

This is not a rejection of what open source gave us. It’s a response to what risks AI is making possible.

We’re still supporting builders, releasing the core code under a new MIT-licensed open source project called cal.diy for hobbyists and tinkerers, but our priority now is simple:

Protecting our customers and community at all costs.

This may not be the most popular call.

But we believe many companies will come to the same conclusion.

My full explanation below ↓
